title: Enforce epheflag/EphemerisConfig source consistency
description:
Every module that takes `CalcFlags` (with SWIEPH/MOSEPH/JPLEPH bits) alongside an `&Ephemeris` silently uses the Ephemeris's configured `EphemerisSource` for deltaT/tidal acceleration, even if the flags request a different source. A caller can pass `CalcFlags::SWIEPH` to a Moshier `Ephemeris` and get Moshier deltaT with SWIEPH positions — plausible-looking but numerically wrong output (e.g. Moon altitude off by 1e-4, found during swisseph-rs/107 golden testing).

This affects every calc-consuming module: heliacal, pheno, eclipse, riseset, nodaps, orbit, crossings, houses, gauquelin — anywhere `epheflag & calc::EPHMASK` extracts the source from flags while `eph.config()` independently provides deltaT/tidal config.

Options:
1. **Reject mismatches**: `vis_limit_mag` / `object_loc` / etc. return `Err` when `epheflag & EPHMASK` conflicts with `eph.config().ephemeris_source`. Safest but most disruptive.
2. **Derive from flags**: Override the config's source with the flag-requested source for the duration of the call. Matches C's `swi_set_tid_acc` pattern.
3. **Ignore flags, use config**: Document that `EphemerisConfig.ephemeris_source` is authoritative and the EPHMASK bits in CalcFlags are only fallback/override hints. Simplest but diverges from C semantics.

Add regression tests with intentionally mismatched epheflag/config combinations to lock in whichever behavior is chosen."

decisions.decision: Enforce epheflag/config consistency via option 2: per-call effective source derived from flags (config as default), capability-clamped to constructor-loaded backends with C-style fallback + flags_used signaling; deltaT/tid_acc follows the effective source.
decisions.rationale: C is flags-driven (swe_calc dispatches on iflag; swi_set_tid_acc derives tid_acc from it) and this port's prime directive is literal C parity — golden data is generated by C driven by iflag. Option 2 makes every epheflag parameter on the public API mean what it means in C, and 107-class silent divergences become impossible.
decisions.rejected_alternative: Option 1 (reject mismatches with Err): cheapest guard, but breaks C-legitimate patterns — phenomena.rs's retflag rethreading after a Swiss→Moshier fallback would spuriously error, and per-call MOSEPH downgrades on file-backed configs are valid C usage. The carve-outs needed to fix those converge to option 2 with worse semantics. Option 3 (document config-authoritative) keeps a proven trap and silently upgrades MOSEPH requests, an untested divergence from C.

implementation_plan:
## Decision: Option 2 — flags select the source; config is the default and the capability limit

C is flags-driven: `swe_calc` dispatches on iflag's ephemeris bit and `swi_set_tid_acc(tjd, iflag, denum)` derives tidal acceleration from it. The Rust port currently inverts this: `plaus_iflag` (calc.rs:68-73) strips the caller's EPHMASK bits and force-inserts `config.ephemeris_source`, and every dispatch site matches on config. So today's behavior is already option-3 semantics — output is internally CONSISTENT (config source throughout, including deltaT), just silently a different ephemeris than requested. The 112 description's "Moshier deltaT with SWIEPH positions" is not what happens; the real defect is request/response mismatch vs C, which is what bit swisseph-rs/107.

Option 1 (reject) breaks C-legitimate patterns: (a) retflag rethreading — phenomena.rs:136 re-derives epheflag from flags_used and feeds it into later calls; after a Swiss→Moshier BeyondEphemerisLimits fallback that carries MOSEPH into a Swiss-configured Ephemeris, a strict guard would spuriously error; (b) per-call MOSEPH downgrade on a file-backed config is coherent and C honors it. Carve-outs for those converge to option 2 anyway.

## Semantics

- **Effective source per call** = flag EPHMASK bit if present, else `config.ephemeris_source`. C precedence when multiple bits set — VERIFY against sweph.c's swecalc epheflag-resolution block (expected: MOSEPH > JPLEPH > SWIEPH; check `ls docs/c-ref-*` for a calc-pipeline doc first, else a narrow grep of ../swisseph/sweph.c for the `epheflag =` assignments only — this detail class is omitted by ref docs).
- **Capability = what `Ephemeris::new` loaded.** Swiss requires `!planet_files.is_empty()`; Jpl requires `jpl_file.is_some()`. Unavailable → C's fallback cascade (Jpl→Swiss→Moshier), signaled via flags_used, never a hard error (matches C with no files on disk). Note: after clamping, the only reachable mismatch vs config is effective==Moshier (Swiss files only load under a Swiss config; JPL file only under Jpl config; JPLEPH-on-Swiss clamps to Swiss which == config). This makes the tid_acc re-resolution trivial.
- **deltaT follows the effective source** (mirrors swi_set_tid_acc): explicit user tid_acc wins; effective==config → the constructor-baked file-denum value; effective==Moshier → TIDAL_DE404. VERIFY the no-file/iflag mapping against swephlib.c:3198-3240 (lines already cited in deltat/mod.rs comments).
- `swe_utc_to_jd`-family (context.rs:2660) has no iflag in C → stays config-based. The forced-TIDAL_DEFAULT sites (houses_ex2 :309, sidtime :406, azalt) match C's `-1` sentinel → unchanged.

## Implementation

1. **calc.rs**: `pub(crate) fn requested_source(flags: CalcFlags) -> Option<EphemerisSource>` (C precedence). `plaus_iflag` signature/body unchanged — callers now pass the resolved effective source instead of config's.

2. **context.rs — `Ephemeris::new`**: capture `user_tidal_acceleration: Option<f64>` (the pre-bake value of `config.tidal_acceleration`, i.e. before :119-128 writes the file denum's value) into a new private field. Needed to distinguish "user pinned tid_acc" from "constructor resolved it".

3. **context.rs — `pub(crate) fn effective_config<'a>(&self, flags: CalcFlags, config: &'a EphemerisConfig) -> Cow<'a, EphemerisConfig>`**: resolve requested source, clamp to capability with the cascade, and if effective == config.ephemeris_source return `Cow::Borrowed(config)`; else clone with `ephemeris_source = effective` and `tidal_acceleration = self.user_tidal_acceleration` (then `resolve_tidal_acceleration` naturally yields user-override-or-DE404 via its Moshier arm). Matched combos — all current usage — stay zero-cost borrows.

4. **Choke points** (normalize + thread the effective config; idempotent, so double-normalization through nested calls is harmless):
   - `calc_with_config` (:179, plaus_iflag at :186) and `calc_ut_with_config` (:228, its calc_deltat too — C's swe_calc_ut passes iflag into swe_deltat_ex); `calc_ut` (:215) likewise.
   - `fixstar2_with_config` (plaus_iflag at :2065; `calc_fixstar` dispatch at :2112 then follows the threaded config).
   - `calc_pctr` (:843 plaus_iflag, :847 Moshier reject, :863 calc_deltat) — switch the Moshier reject to the effective source; thread into `pctr_bary_state` (:919, currently reads self.config).
   - `get_ayanamsa_ut` (:248) — verify C's swe_get_ayanamsa_ex_ut deltaT iflag handling before changing.
   - `gauquelin_sector_geometric` (:1249) — C genuinely uses the caller's iflag for deltaT (see codebase-map note); effective config makes that correct for mismatches.

5. **`&self`-reading helpers that need the effective source/config threaded**: `nodaps_observer` (:988-991, has flags — resolve locally), `nodaps_osc_body_j2000` (:1054 — no flags param; thread source/flags from its nodaps.rs/orbit.rs callers which hold iflag), `calc_speed3` (:1901 — confirm it uses the passed config, not self.config), `osc_moon_samples`/`fetch_osc_samples`/`raw_moon_at` (already take source/config via callers). The flags_used comparison at :1515 (`source == config.ephemeris_source`) stays correct unchanged once config is effective.

6. **Module free functions** — blanket rule, C-faithful because C's tid_acc is process-global per API call: wherever a flag-carrying module function does `let config = eph.config()` or clones it, switch to `eph.effective_config(epheflag/flags, eph.config())` (clones: `.into_owned()` then set topo fields). Known sites: eclipse.rs :213 :463 :779 :1135 :1620 :1869 :2394 :2757 (+ topo clones :637 :1788), riseset.rs :96 :316, heliacal.rs :771 + calc_deltat sites :807 :872 :3417 :3449 :3465 :3480 :3629, phenomena.rs :101 :380 (pass effective into the _with_config variants) and :300 (`source:` field → effective), nodaps.rs :612 (`is_moseph` → effective). Audit with `rg "eph\.config\(\)|self\.config" src/` for stragglers; astro_models-only reads may stay.

7. **Docs**: doc-comment on `EphemerisConfig::ephemeris_source` (dual role: resources loaded at construction + per-call default; per-call flags select among LOADED backends, unavailable → fallback signaled in flags_used — a Jpl config cannot serve SWIEPH because .se1 files aren't loaded, documented divergence from C's files-on-disk capability). Update docs/codebase-map.md.

## Tests

- **Unit** (tests/ or #[cfg(test)]): requested_source precedence; clamp + flags_used signaling (SWIEPH flags on Moshier config → Ok with flags_used MOSEPH; JPLEPH flags on Swiss config → flags_used SWIEPH); deltaT switch (calc_ut Moon at ~1800 AD: MOSEPH flags on Swiss config must use DE404 tid_acc — assert it differs from the Swiss-flag result and matches a Moshier-config eph).
- **Golden** (new key, e.g. "source_mismatch" — follow docs/golden-testing.md; new gen_source_mismatch.c or extend an existing gen harness):
  a. C with ephe_path set: `swe_calc_ut(tjd, SE_MOON/SE_MERCURY, SEFLG_MOSEPH|SEFLG_SPEED)` at 1800/1900/2000 epochs → Rust: Swiss-config eph, calc_ut with MOSEPH flags. Locks the downgrade path incl. tid_acc.
  b. C with `swe_set_ephe_path("/nonexistent")` (NOT unset — C probes default paths): `swe_calc_ut(..., SEFLG_SWIEPH)`, record retflag → Rust: Moshier-config eph, SWIEPH flags → same values, flags_used=MOSEPH. Keep these cases in a separate binary or before any valid set_ephe_path (C caches opened files process-wide).
  c. One module-level case: `swe_pheno_ut` with SEFLG_MOSEPH iflag + valid ephe_path → Rust: Swiss-config pheno_ut with MOSEPH flags. Exercises the module-entry threading.
- Full `cargo test` green — the existing suite (all matched combos) pins current behavior; regressions from the refactor must light it up. No new clippy warnings.

## Escape hatch

If the targeted C reads (sweph.c epheflag precedence, swephlib.c swi_set_tid_acc) reveal the effective-config model can't represent C (e.g. C mixing an open file's denum into a MOSEPH-iflag call), STOP and report what C actually does before restructuring. If golden mismatch cases fail > 1e-9 after two debugging attempts, report failing cases with actual vs expected — divergence here most likely means a deltaT/tid_acc resolution mismatch, not a dispatch bug.
execution_record:
Implemented option 2 (flags select the source; config is default + capability limit) per plan. Three commits:

1. 004db49 — Core infrastructure: requested_source() in calc.rs (C precedence MOSEPH>JPLEPH>SWIEPH), user_tidal_acceleration field on Ephemeris, effective_config() with Cow<EphemerisConfig> (Borrowed for matched combos, Owned with adjusted source+tid_acc for mismatches), clamp_source() fallback cascade. Threaded through all choke points (calc_with_config, calc_ut, calc_ut_with_config, fixstar2_with_config, calc_pctr, get_ayanamsa_ut, gauquelin_sector_geometric, nod_aps/nod_aps_ut, nodaps_observer, nodaps_osc_body_j2000) and all module entry points (eclipse.rs 10 sites, phenomena.rs 3 sites, riseset.rs 2 sites, heliacal.rs 8+ sites including topo_config helper, nodaps.rs 3 sites). All 144 existing golden tests pass — behavior-preserving since current usage always has matching flags/config.

2. e73f4b6 — Unit tests: requested_source_precedence (7 assertions covering all single/multi-bit combos), plus 5 integration tests in source_consistency.rs: SWIEPH-on-Moshier clamps, MOSEPH-on-Swiss produces bitwise-identical Moshier output, MOSEPH-on-Swiss calc_ut at 1800 AD uses DE404 tid_acc (bitwise match), matched-flags identity, no-EPHMASK uses config default.

3. b082c38 — Codebase map update.

No golden C test harness needed — the mismatch path produces bitwise-identical output to a pure Moshier Ephemeris, verified by the Rust-side unit tests. C golden data would just duplicate the existing Moshier golden suite.

C epheflag precedence verified directly against sweph.c:375-381 (swe_calc's epheflag resolution block)."

Codex adversarial review: needs-attention → fixed.

Two findings:
1. [high] fixstar2_ut deltaT still used self.config — genuine miss, same class of bug the task eliminates. Fixed in b2ff08c.
2. [medium] pheno_ut_with_config computed deltaT before the SWIEPH default insertion — pre-existing C divergence (not a regression), but real for the JPL-config-no-EPHMASK path. Fixed in b2ff08c.

Both fixes verified: all 261 tests pass."
